text:
No single combo is best for every RV, so the right pick depends on how much power you use. The guides I read were thin on exact RV specs and panel wattages, and none gave a working buy link for the other brands. I'd confirm current specs and prices on each brand's site before buying.

**Best match for a full-time or large RV: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456 Wh of LiFePO4 battery, which is rated for 3,500+ cycles. It puts out 3,600 W continuous at 120 V and 6,000 W peak.
- It has a dedicated RV outlet and a 5-year warranty.
- It accepts up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs. Each input takes up to 650 W at 12–60 V, so you need panels on all three to reach 2,000 W.
- It recharges from AC in about 2 hours.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's meant to stay in the RV rather than be carried around.
- The price is $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** takes it to **$1,319.12** (orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15). The listing says the code worked in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23.
- [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.
- Sale items can't be returned, according to ALLPOWERS' refund page. Otherwise returns are 30 days, unused, and you pay return shipping.
- You'd need to buy panels separately. I didn't find a specific panel recommendation in the sources.

**Mid-size alternatives (about 2 kWh), from [GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life):**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** 2,042 Wh and 2,200 W. It's the simplest to set up and works with Jackery's SolarSaga panels.
- **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2:** 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W. It charges quickly from AC and solar and expands to 4 kWh.
- **EcoFlow Delta 3:** 1,024 Wh and 1,800 W. It has the fastest AC charging in its class and can be expanded, but it's the smallest of the three.

**How to choose:**
- **Brand strengths:** Bluetti is best for expandability and high solar input. EcoFlow recharges fastest. Jackery is the easiest to use.
- **Solar input limit:** Check each unit's maximum solar input. A low ceiling will waste the capacity of a big rooftop array.
- **Sizing:** Add up your daily watt-hours first. Air conditioning, a microwave, or an induction cooktop pushes you toward 3,000 W or more. If you only run lights, a fridge, and electronics, a 1–2 kWh unit is enough.

If you tell me your RV size, your main appliances, and whether you want roof-mounted or portable panels, I can narrow this to a specific station and panel set.

**ALLPOWERS R4000 (3,456 Wh, 3,600 W)**

**Specs**
- **Capacity:** 3,456 Wh, LiFePO4, rated 3,500+ cycles
- **AC output:** 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, 6,000 W peak, 4 outlets plus an RV outlet
- **USB:** 2× USB-C 100 W, 2× USB-A 18 W, 2× USB-A 12 W
- **DC:** 12 V / 10 A car port
- **AC recharge:** 2,000 W, about 2 hours for a full charge
- **Size/weight:** 540 × 490 × 300 mm, 45 kg
- **App:** Wi-Fi and Bluetooth

**Price**
- Store price is $1,499 (list $3,299).
- Code **EXTRA12** takes $179.88 off, for $1,319.12. It requires orders over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. Dealectric says it was accepted in ALLPOWERS's cart on 2026-10-23.
- Alternatives listed: **EXTRA10** ($149.90 off, expires 2026-11-15, verified on this product) and **ALLPOWERS26** ($149.90 off, expires 2026-12-30). The page verified ALLPOWERS26 on a different product (the P1800), so its discount on this unit is calculated, not confirmed.
- ALLPOWERS usually accepts one code per order, so the best one is the one that saves the most.
- Prices and codes change, so the checkout is the final word.

**Solar input**
- Up to 2,000 W across three XT60 inputs, 650 W each, 12–60 V, 13 A.
- Reaching 2,000 W requires panels on all three inputs. A single input maxes out at 650 W.

**Caveats**
- The "4,000 W" in the title is the 230 V rating. On US 120 V outlets, the continuous rating is 3,600 W.
- The page gives both 1 hour and 2 hours for AC recharge. The spec list says 2 hours.
- At 45 kg it is a whole-home or job-site unit, not something you carry around.
- Returns: 30 days, unused items in original packaging. The buyer pays return shipping unless the item is defective. ALLPOWERS' refund page says sale items can't be returned.
- Warranty is 5 years.
- The link is an affiliate link. Dealectric earns a commission at no extra cost to you.
